5.q: Trace the correct sequence of cross-demand effects when a tax raises the price of sugary aerated drinks.
5.a: The chain runs: (1) The tax raises the price of aerated drinks (2) Fruit juices become relatively cheaper as substitute goods (3) Consumers switch toward juices and demand rises (4) The juice demand curve shifts rightward at every juice price. A wrong answer that predicts the same rise for a complementary good such as fast food shows the student has reversed the cross-demand rule that complements move opposite to the related good's price while substitutes move together.
